problem.title: Design a Write-Optimized LSM-Tree Storage Engine
problem.prompt: Design a single-node embedded key-value storage engine (similar to RocksDB or LevelDB) capable of sustaining 250,000 random writes/sec of 1 KB payloads while bounding p99 point-lookup latency under 8 ms and preventing unbounded disk growth from overwrites and tombstones.
requirements: Support Put(key, value), Get(key), Delete(key), and ordered RangeScan(startKey, endKey) with crash durability.
Sustain 250,000 random writes/sec (250 MB/s) without triggering random 4 KB in-place page updates on disk.
Bound p99 point-lookup latency to <= 8 ms even across 10 TB of stored data and 90% negative lookups.
Reclaim space from overwritten keys and delete tombstones via background compaction without stalling foreground writers.
constraints: RAM budget is capped at 16 GB (max 256 MB for active/immutable MemTables; remainder for block cache and Bloom filters).
Storage is NVMe SSD (3.5 GB/s sequential write, 80,000 random read IOPS, 120 us 4 KB read latency).
Crash recovery from WAL must complete in under 10 seconds after an unclean process kill.

stages.learnerPrompt: Before designing the engine, explain why a B+Tree struggles at 250,000 random 1 KB writes/sec and how an LSM-tree flips the I/O profile.

referenceMaterial.summary: A B+Tree performs random 16 KB page reads and dirty-page flushes on random keys, exhausting 80,000 NVMe random IOPS. An LSM-tree batches writes in a sequential WAL and RAM SkipList, flushing 64 MB sorted runs sequentially.
approachSteps: Quantify random IOPS bottleneck: 250k writes/sec exceeds 80k SSD random IOPS when buffer pool hit rate drops.
Contrast in-place page mutation (B+Tree) with append-only sequential WAL + immutable SSTables (LSM-tree).
Identify the three amplification metrics: Write Amplification (WA), Read Amplification (RA), and Space Amplification (SA).
tradeOffs: B+Tree offers O(log N) read amplification (1 tree traversal) vs LSM-tree checking MemTable + L0 + L1..Ln.
LSM-tree achieves 10x-50x higher random write throughput at the cost of background compaction CPU and I/O.
alternatives: B+Tree with large NVMe write-back cache (still hits random flush wall at 10 TB).
Hash-indexed Bitcask (requires all keys to fit in RAM, violating 16 GB limit for 10B keys).
failureModes: Forgetting descending seqNum sorting causes Get() to return stale overwritten values.

stages.learnerPrompt: Sketch the write path (WAL + MemTable), SSTable layout with Bloom filters, and the leveled compaction strategy. Include capacity numbers for your 16 GB RAM budget.
Implement the core MemTable flush and point-lookup path across MemTable, L0 Bloom filters, and leveled SSTables.

referenceMaterial.summary: Core Java implementation of the LSM write path (WAL group commit + SkipList MemTable) and point lookup checking MemTable, L0 Bloom filters, and non-overlapping L1+ SSTables.
approachSteps: Append to WAL with CRC32C and insert into ConcurrentSkipListMap.
Swap active MemTable to immutable queue at 64 MB and flush asynchronously.
On Get(key), probe MemTable -> Immutable MemTables -> L0 (all files, Bloom-filtered) -> L1..Ln (binary search file range, Bloom-filtered, binary search sparse index).
tradeOffs: Reference-counted Version snapshots avoid reader/compactor locks at the cost of delaying file deletion until active reads finish.
alternatives: Partitioned index/filter blocks cached in the 14.5 GB LRU block cache instead of pinning all Bloom filters in RAM.
failureModes: Skipping Bloom filter or checking L0 oldest-first returns stale values or wastes NVMe IOPS.

stages.learnerPrompt: Compare Leveled Compaction vs. Size-Tiered Compaction for this 10 TB, 16 GB RAM workload. Why is Leveled Compaction chosen here?

referenceMaterial.summary: Leveled Compaction bounds space amplification to ~1.1x (critical at 10 TB) and limits L1-L6 lookup fan-out to 1 SSTable per level, whereas Size-Tiered Compaction can spike to 2x space amplification (10 TB wasted) and high read amplification.
approachSteps: Compare Space Amplification: Leveled (~1.1x) vs Size-Tiered (~2.0x during major compaction).
Compare Read Amplification: Leveled (L0 + 1 file per level) vs Size-Tiered (multiple overlapping tiers).
Mitigate Leveled Write Amplification (~10-12x) using LZ4 compression and parallel subcompactions.
tradeOffs: Leveled compaction saves ~9 TB of SSD capacity vs Size-Tiered, at the cost of 3x higher compaction write volume.
alternatives: FIFO compaction for strict TTL time-series data with no updates/deletes.
Tiered + Leveled hybrid (L0-L2 tiered, L3-L6 leveled).
failureModes: Disabling compression during L0->L6 compaction causes internal I/O (3.0 GB/s) to saturate the 3.5 GB/s NVMe link.

stages.learnerPrompt: What happens when a sudden 500k writes/sec burst hits the engine, or when a bulk delete leaves 50M consecutive tombstones?

referenceMaterial.summary: Unchecked bursts cause L0 pileups and write stalls; massive tombstone ranges degrade range scans. Both require backpressure rate-limiting and tombstone-aware compaction scoring.
approachSteps: Apply soft write throttling at 12 L0 files and hard stall at 24 L0 files.
Track tombstone count in SSTable properties and boost compaction priority when tombstones > 20%.
Support RangeTombstones (`DeleteRange`) so a single marker covers millions of keys.
tradeOffs: Soft throttling adds 20-240 us per write during bursts to prevent multi-second hard write stalls.
alternatives: Dynamic level-size base adjustment to match actual bottom-level size.
failureModes: Dropping tombstones before the bottommost level (L6) resurrects deleted keys from deeper SSTables.

stages.learnerPrompt: How would you extend this single-node LSM-tree to separate compute from storage on S3/object storage, or reduce CPU overhead via key-value separation (WiscKey)?

referenceMaterial.summary: Key-value separation (WiscKey) stores only keys and 16-byte value pointers in the LSM-tree while keeping large values in an append-only vLog, slashing compaction write amplification by 10x+.
approachSteps: Store `(valueLogFileId, offset, length)` in the SSTable when `value.length > 1 KB`.
Run asynchronous vLog garbage collection to relocate live values and reclaim tail space.
For cloud-native storage, persist immutable SSTables and MANIFEST directly to S3 with local NVMe read caching.
tradeOffs: WiscKey cuts compaction I/O dramatically for large values (> 1 KB) but adds an extra random NVMe read on RangeScan.
alternatives: RocksDB BlobDB integrated directly into compaction.
failureModes: vLog garbage collection falling behind under high overwrite rates exhausts disk space despite small LSM levels.

spark.summary: Convert random key-value writes into sequential append-only disk I/O using an in-memory MemTable, a durable WAL, immutable SSTables, and background leveled compaction.
spark.keyTakeaway: LSM-trees trade read amplification and background compaction CPU/I/O for 10x-50x higher random write throughput than B+Trees on SSDs and HDDs.

problem.title: Design a Write-Optimized LSM-Tree Storage Engine
problem.prompt: Design a single-node embedded key-value storage engine (similar to RocksDB or LevelDB) capable of sustaining 250,000 random writes/sec of 1 KB payloads while bounding p99 point-lookup latency under 8 ms and preventing unbounded disk growth from overwrites and tombstones.
requirements: Support Put(key, value), Get(key), Delete(key), and ordered RangeScan(startKey, endKey) with crash durability.
Sustain 250,000 random writes/sec (250 MB/s) without triggering random 4 KB in-place page updates on disk.
Bound p99 point-lookup latency to <= 8 ms even across 10 TB of stored data and 90% negative lookups.
Reclaim space from overwritten keys and delete tombstones via background compaction without stalling foreground writers.
constraints: RAM budget is capped at 16 GB (max 256 MB for active/immutable MemTables; remainder for block cache and Bloom filters).
Storage is NVMe SSD (3.5 GB/s sequential write, 80,000 random read IOPS, 120 us 4 KB read latency).
Crash recovery from WAL must complete in under 10 seconds after an unclean process kill.

concept.whyItMatters: Traditional B+Trees perform in-place 4 KB or 16 KB page mutations, causing severe random I/O write amplification and page-split lock contention under write-heavy telemetry, time-series, and event-logging workloads. LSM-trees buffer mutations in memory and flush sorted immutable runs sequentially, saturating NVMe bandwidth while keeping space overhead predictable.
whenToUse: Write-heavy workloads (> 50% writes or high ingestion rates) such as time-series metrics, observability logs, and message queues.
Datasets where keys are inserted in random order (UUIDs, hashes) that would thrash a B+Tree buffer pool.
Workloads that benefit from high compression ratios on immutable, prefix-compressed sorted blocks.
whenNotToUse: Read-heavy point-lookup workloads with strict sub-millisecond tail latency where compaction I/O jitter is unacceptable.
Small datasets that fit entirely in RAM where a lock-free B+Tree or hash index avoids compaction complexity.
keyPoints: Writes append sequentially to an on-disk Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with group commit and insert into an in-memory SkipList MemTable.
Once a MemTable hits 64 MB, it freezes into an Immutable MemTable and flushes asynchronously to an L0 SSTable with 4 KB data blocks, a sparse index, and a 10-bit/key Bloom filter.
Point lookups check MemTable -> Immutable MemTables -> all L0 SSTables (overlapping key ranges) -> at most one SSTable per level L1..Ln.
Leveled compaction bounds space amplification (~1.1x) and read amplification at the cost of 10x-30x write amplification.
terms: MemTable: An in-memory ordered data structure (typically a concurrent SkipList) that buffers recent writes before flushing to disk.
SSTable (Sorted String Table): An immutable disk file storing sorted key-value pairs in 4 KB compressed blocks with a trailing sparse index and Bloom filter.
Tombstone: A special deletion marker written to the MemTable and SSTables so older versions in lower levels are masked until compaction.

tradeOffs.pro: Leveled compaction keeps non-overlapping key ranges per level (L1+), bounding space amplification to ~1.1x and point-lookup fan-out to 1 SSTable per level.
tradeOffs.con: Leveled compaction rewrites data ~10x per level transition, increasing SSD wear and write amplification to 10x-30x compared to 2x-5x for size-tiered.

tradeOffs.factor: Bloom Filter Bits per Key (10 bits vs. 14 bits)
tradeOffs.pro: 10 bits/key yields a ~1% false positive rate while consuming only 1.25 GB RAM per 1 billion keys.
tradeOffs.con: Raising to 14 bits/key drops false positives to ~0.12% but consumes 40% more block-cache RAM that could otherwise cache hot index/data blocks.

failureModes.name: L0 Write Stall / Compaction Debt
failureModes.description: Foreground writes outpace L0->L1 compaction, piling up > 20 overlapping L0 SSTables and forcing the engine to throttle or block all incoming writes.
failureModes.mitigation: Cap L0 file count (soft throttle at 12 files, hard stop at 24), parallelize L1+ subcompactions across CPU cores, and rate-limit compaction I/O.

failureModes.name: Tombstone Read Amplification
failureModes.description: Range scans over millions of recently deleted keys must skip through dense tombstones across L0-L3 before finding live keys, spiking p99 scan latency.
failureModes.mitigation: Emit range-delete tombstones, track tombstone density in SSTable metadata, and prioritize compacting SSTables with > 20% tombstones.

failureModes.name: Torn WAL Record on Power Loss
failureModes.description: A partial write during an OS crash leaves a corrupted trailing record in the active WAL segment, halting startup replay.
failureModes.mitigation: Include a CRC32C checksum and length header per 32 KB WAL block; during recovery, truncate at the first checksum mismatch.

commonMistakes: Performing in-place deletes on SSTables instead of appending tombstones, which breaks immutability and requires rewriting entire files on every delete.
Calling fsync() individually on every Put() instead of batching concurrent writers via WAL group commit, capping throughput at ~2,000 IOPS.
Forgetting to check all L0 SSTables on Get() because L0 files have overlapping key ranges unlike L1+.
Deleting old SSTables before the new compacted SSTable and updated MANIFEST file are fsynced, risking data loss on crash.

sections.content:
## The Core Problem

At **250,000 random 1 KB writes/sec** (250 MB/s raw payload), a B+Tree must read 16 KB leaf pages from disk, dirty them in the buffer pool, and flush random 16 KB pages back to NVMe. Even with a 50% cache hit rate, random page flushing saturates 80,000 IOPS and triggers severe SSD internal garbage collection.

An **LSM-tree** eliminates random disk writes by turning every `Put` and `Delete` into two fast operations:
1. Sequential append to a **Write-Ahead Log (WAL)** for durability.
2. In-memory insert into a **SkipList MemTable** ($O(\log N)$).

The challenge shifts from write latency to **controlling read amplification** (checking multiple sorted runs) and **compaction write amplification** (merging runs without stalling writers).

## Requirements & Constraints

- **Write Throughput:** 250,000 writes/sec @ 1 KB avg payload = **250 MB/s** sustained ingestion.
- **Point Lookup Latency:** p99 **<= 8 ms** across **10 TB** total data (~10 billion 1 KB keys), including negative lookups (`Get` on missing keys).
- **Memory Ceiling:** **16 GB RAM** total:
  - 256 MB reserved for 1 active + up to 3 immutable 64 MB MemTables.
  - ~1.25 GB for Bloom filters (10 bits/key on 1B hot/warm keys or partitioned index/filter blocks).
  - ~14.5 GB for 4 KB LRU Block Cache.
- **Recovery SLA:** Unclean crash replay from WAL must finish in **< 10 s**.

## Capacity & Amplification Math

- **MemTable Flush Frequency:** At 250 MB/s ingestion and 64 MB MemTable size, a flush occurs every `64 / 250 = 0.256 s` (~4 flushes/sec).
- **WAL Size & Replay:** With 4 immutable MemTables max, the active un-flushed WAL spans at most `64 MB * 2 = 128 MB`. Replaying 128 MB sequentially from NVMe at 3.5 GB/s + CPU SkipList insertion (~400 MB/s) finishes in **< 0.5 s**, well under the 10 s SLA.
- **Leveled Compaction Hierarchy (10x level multiplier):**
  - `L0`: max 4 files x 64 MB = 256 MB (overlapping key ranges)
  - `L1`: 256 MB (non-overlapping)
  - `L2`: 2.56 GB
  - `L3`: 25.6 GB
  - `L4`: 256 GB
  - `L5`: 2.56 TB
  - `L6`: ~10 TB
- **Write Amplification:** Moving a byte from L0 to L6 with 10x fan-out rewrites it ~10x per level across 6 levels (~30x total worst-case, ~12x with sub-compactions and compression).
- **Compaction Disk Bandwidth:** `250 MB/s * 12 = 3.0 GB/s` peak internal I/O (or `1.5 GB/s` write + `1.5 GB/s` read), fitting inside a 3.5 GB/s NVMe drive only if LZ4 compression (~2x) is enabled (`1.5 GB/s` compressed I/O).

sections.content:
## Detailed Component Design

### 1. Group-Commit WAL & Concurrent MemTable
- Multiple writer threads enqueue `(key, value, seqNum)` into a lock-free queue. A single leader batches up to 64 writes (or 200 us window), writes one contiguous 32 KB CRC32C-framed block to the WAL, calls `fdatasync()`, and then inserts into a `ConcurrentSkipListMap` (or Arena-backed SkipList).
- Each key is stored as an **InternalKey**: `(userKey, seqNum DESC, opType)` so newer sequence numbers sort first.

### 2. SSTable Binary Layout
- **Data Blocks (4 KB uncompressed, LZ4 compressed):** Prefix-encoded keys with restart points every 16 keys for fast intra-block binary search.
- **Filter Block:** 10-bit/key Bloom filter using double-hashing (`h1 + i * h2`) to reject 99% of negative lookups in RAM.
- **Index Block:** Stores `(lastKeyInBlock, offset, size)` for every 4 KB data block.
- **Footer (48 bytes):** Magic number + offsets for Index and MetaIndex blocks.

### 3. Crash-Safe Compaction & MANIFEST
- Compaction reads input SSTables via sequential `pread()` (bypassing OS page cache with `O_DIRECT` to prevent cache pollution), performs a min-heap k-way merge, drops stale `seqNum` duplicates, and drops tombstones only when compacting into the bottommost level (`L6`).
- New SSTables are `fsync()`-ed, then a single atomic `VersionEdit` record is appended and `fsync()`-ed to the `MANIFEST` log before unlinking old SSTables.

## Failure Handling & Edge Cases

- **Write Stalls:** If L0 reaches 12 files, apply a dynamic rate limiter (e.g., 50 us sleep per write) to give compaction threads headroom; hard-block at 24 L0 files to avoid unbounded read latency.
- **Read-During-Compaction:** Readers acquire an atomic reference-counted `SuperVersion` snapshot. Old SSTables remain unlinked only after the last reader releases its `SuperVersion`.
- **Clock Skew / Sequence Numbers:** Never use wall-clock timestamps for version ordering; use a monotonically increasing 64-bit `seqNum` persisted in `MANIFEST` and WAL headers.

## Final Architecture Summary

1. **Write Path:** Group-committed CRC32C WAL + 64 MB SkipList MemTable sustains 250k writes/sec via pure sequential I/O.
2. **Read Path:** Check MemTable -> Immutable MemTables -> L0 Bloom filters -> 1 binary-searched SSTable per level (L1-L6) via 14.5 GB LRU Block Cache, keeping p99 `Get` under 2-5 ms.
3. **Compaction:** Multi-threaded leveled compaction with LZ4 compression and `O_DIRECT` keeps space amplification at ~1.1x and bounds write amplification within NVMe bandwidth.

options.text: Dropping tombstones before the bottommost level (L6) resurrects deleted keys from deeper SSTables.
